applies_why: The judge text gives an UNDERDETERMINED verdict on a chain argument, so the rule governing grounds for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED applies.
quote: while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: The phrase 'That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for ... UNDERDETERMINED' required deciding whether 'neither chain forces the other' is forbidden single-verse silence or a permissible chain stalemate; the two readings are (1) it rests on Acts 2:30 not naming Joseph and is forbidden, or (2) it weighs two chains and finds no forcing support and is allowed.
why: The judge's stated ground is a stalemate between two chains, not that a single verse does not state the link, so K-S2 does not make this UNDERDETERMINED a breach.
